# omx-dsp / fuzz_note_map

omx-dsp's own fuzz target `fuzz_note_map` ([source](source/fuzz_note_map.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-dsp 0.27.0 (FreeMixer/omx-dsp at a0ee1dfe).

Builds a valid note leg (channel, key range, transpose, velocity curve, fixed velocity) from six bytes. It then runs records until the input ends: three raw MIDI bytes through the map, a set_leg with six raw ints (or a valid leg from bytes), or a release_all with a cap of 1 to 4. A model of the downstream synth's sounding notes, the harness's own copy of the leg in force and its own table of held keys check each output. At the end it releases everything and checks every velocity curve.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libomxdsp.a, which build.sh compiles from omx-dsp's five src/*.c files with -DOMX_CONTRACTS and -ffp-contract=off; the note map is inline in omx_note_map.h. The Makefile's own fuzz build uses native clang with libFuzzer, which this build replaces with the standard driver.
- omx-contract's headers are pinned to the tag v3.4.0 (1169c701), where the library's Makefile uses whichever omx-contract is installed, at or above its packaging floor of 3.1.0.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- A call writes no more messages than it has room for. Each message is a channel message with 7-bit data bytes, a note on has a velocity of 1 or more on a channel the leg takes, and a note off is for a key the model has sounding ([lines 87-128](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L87-L128)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The leg the harness builds from the first bytes is one the library accepts as valid ([lines 146-152](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L146-L152)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A note on that the leg takes, with a transposed key inside 0..127, is delivered. Every delivered note on is inside the leg's key range and makes one message, or two when its key was held. The last message sounds the transposed key, and out_of_range equals the harness's own count ([lines 177-211](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L177-L211)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- set_leg accepts a leg exactly when the harness's own reading finds it valid. An accepted leg becomes the policy, and a refused one leaves the old policy ([lines 231-244](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L231-L244)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- release_all writes no more than its cap and only note offs. Afterwards nothing is held and the model has nothing sounding ([lines 251-287](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L251-L287)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each record, held_count equals the held table's population, and the table holds as many keys as the harness's own count of what was played ([lines 289-302](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L289-L302)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The release at the end of the input leaves nothing held and no note sounding in the model ([lines 310-325](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L310-L325)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every velocity curve maps each velocity 1..127 into 1..127, and the linear curve is the identity ([lines 330-344](source/fuzz_note_map.c#L330-L344)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- At the end of the input, no contract of the library is recorded as broken ([lines 160-168](source/fuzz.h#L160-L168)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch omx-dsp` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

|---|---|---:|---|

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
